transcript_text:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-20
- Time: 16:00 PT
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Priya (Lagoon CTO), Ben (Lead ML Eng), Zoe (Product)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
Lagoon Labs is evaluating Redwood for a user-facing summarization feature. They want fastest path to 'first call' with self-serve credits but also have questions around VPC/private deployment for production. Key risks: data residency, SSO, and latency vs cost tradeoffs. Next steps: send security docs; schedule perf demo; share credits guide.

Topics: quickstart credits, time-to-first-token, hosted vs dedicated vs private, VPC peering, SOC2/KMS, lat/cost, canary rollouts

Action items (captured inline, also in metadata): Maya/Carlos items and Ben to provide target load numbers.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Maya from Redwood... Carlos, you on?
[00:09] Carlos: Yep here, hi all. Quick note I'm the SE, I'll walk perf and infra details.
[00:15] Priya: Thanks. We're excited; short intros? I'm Priya, CTO at Lagoon Labs, we do near-real-time document summarization for B2B customers.
[00:25] Ben: Ben, I lead the ML infra team. Our main questions are time-to-first-token for prod, and whether we can start with self-serve credits.
[00:34] Zoe: Zoe on product. Focused on product metrics and rollout gating.
[00:38] Maya: Great. Today we'll cover the quickstart path to first call using hosted Redwood API, what free credits look like, and then when you'd consider Dedicated or Private. We'll also touch security (SOC2 / SSO / KMS) and VPC networking.
[00:52] Priya: Perfect. Our priority is to ship a minimal public beta within 3 weeks. We need to know realistically how fast we can get to a testable integration.
[01:05] Carlos: For self-serve hosted, you can be calling the API within minutes: sign up, redeem credits, get API key. In practice, for a simple summarization endpoint we see teams hit first call in under an hour including SDK install, but depends on how you handle streaming and tokens.
[01:25] Ben: When you say 'under an hour', is that with streaming and chunking? Our encoder outputs variable length, lots of 2k token calls.
[01:34] Carlos: Good question. We usually recommend a couple of quick things: 1) smaller chunking pre prompts to keep seq lengths predictable, 2) enable prefix KV cache if you have repeated contexts, 3) test a couple model variants. For hosted you're hitting Redwood-managed kernels so no infra work.
[01:58] Priya: For the public beta, we don't want any PII to leave our VPC. Is that an immediate blocker?
[02:07] Maya: Not necessarily. Many customers start with hosted for beta with contract-level data retention rules and can use response scrubbing. If you need full air-gapped control, Private is the end-state. There's a middle ground: Dedicated capacity with VPC peering and customer-managed encryption keys.
[02:29] Zoe: VPC peering sounds interesting. How does that affect time to prod?
[02:34] Carlos: VPC peering adds some setup: networking ACLs, peer approval, and routing. Expect 1-2 weeks for Dedicated with VPC peering depending on your infra team bandwidth. For private on-prem it's longer — multiple weeks to months.
[02:56] Ben: Latency is a big one. For our UX, 95th percentile under 700ms is ideal. Can Redwood meet that on hosted?
[03:06] Carlos: Depends on model size and region. For mid-size open models we commonly see p95s in 300-600ms for short responses. When you add long seqs, or heavy context, lat increases. Dedicated capacity tuned to your workload is where you get consistent p95 guarantees.
[03:25] Priya: And pricing — do credits map to tokens at same rate as production billing?
[03:31] Maya: Credits are structured to let you prototype; they correspond roughly to tokens but may have promo conversion. We'll share the credits guide with exact math. For planning, assume hosted per-token pricing, and Dedicated is via reserved capacity commit.
[03:47] Ben: Any friction with SSO? We use Okta and SAML.
[03:51] Maya: We support SAML SSO for the console and RBAC. For API keys you can integrate via your secrets manager and KMS; Redwood supports customer KMS for Private and Dedicated, and BYOK in Private.
[04:07] Zoe: Can you run simple canary rollouts? We want to test model changes gradually.
[04:12] Carlos: Yep rollouts are built-in: canary and A/B routing, automatic fallback to a cheaper variant on failures. That's the same in hosted and Dedicated; in Private it's in the control plane we ship.
[04:28] Priya: Ok the dev team will want sample code. How opinionated are your SDKs? We want plain curl or python example.
[04:36] Maya: We'll send both. Carlos will attach a quickstart repo with curl, python snippets, and a sample streaming handler.
[04:44] Ben: For our test workload, we expect bursts — up to 50 qps sustained for 30 minutes. Any advice?
[04:52] Carlos: For bursty workloads, autoscaling on Dedicated helps. Hosted does have rate limits per account but we can adjust for pilots. For predictable throughput, Dedicated reserved pools are best. Also consider batching at the app layer for small requests.
[05:10] Priya: Are there any gotchas with KV cache? I heard it called KV cash in one talk, lol.
[05:16] Carlos: (laughs) Yeah KV cache — it's the token-level key/value cache for autoregressive models. If you have lots of repeated context it saves tokens and latency. We'll include guidelines for cache TTL and sharding.
[05:32] Zoe: Security docs — do you have SOC2 type 2 and ISO stuff?
[05:36] Maya: We have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 reports; we'll send the summary and contact for security review. For audit logs and retention we support per-tenant logs and configurable retention windows.
[05:50] Ben: Encryption at rest — do you manage keys or can we bring our own?
[05:54] Carlos: Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default. Dedicated supports customer KMS via cloud KMS; Private supports HSM/BYOK.
[06:06] Priya: Great. On the credits: is there a way to auto-apply credits when we sign up, or does someone at Redwood have to enable it?
[06:15] Maya: For standard PLG credits, you can redeem via the console. For larger pilot credits we may provision them on our side; I'll coordinate that.
[06:24] Zoe: Anything we should measure pre/post integration to watch quality regressions?
[06:29] Carlos: We recommend prompt-set based evals: track rouge/bertscore/type-specific metrics and integrate Redwood Optimize to monitor regression alerts. We'll share a sample eval harness.
[06:45] Priya: What about data residency — our EU customers need data stored in EU.
[06:51] Maya: We have region-aware routing. Hosted supports EU regions; you can pin requests to EU. For stronger guarantees, Dedicated in EU or Private on-prem is the path.
[07:04] Ben: For the performance demo later, can we run a bench with our model or do you require using Redwood-curated models?
[07:12] Carlos: We can run benchmarks with your model bundle in Dedicated or Private. For hosted, we generally benchmark our curated model catalog. For accurate numbers on your model we recommend a Dedicated pilot or Private deployment.
[07:27] Zoe: If we start with hosted for beta and then move to Dedicated, how smooth is the migration?
[07:33] Maya: We aim for a consistent API + config layer so migrations are smooth: pin model versions, rollout policies carry over. There might be infra-specific tuning (quantization or kernel choices).
[07:48] Priya: Do you support per-route cost attribution? We want to see per-feature spend.
[07:54] Carlos: Yes Console shows token-level cost and per-route breakdowns, and tracing for latency. We'll show screenshots in the follow-up.
[08:05] Ben: Ok for action items — we'll gather our target p95/p50, and expected QPS. Any specific formats?
[08:12] Carlos: A spreadsheet with endpoints, avg tokens in/out, target p50/p95, and concurrency targets is ideal. We'll use that for a perf runbook.
[08:23] Priya: Can you clarify the timeline differences: hosted = minutes to hours, Dedicated = 1-2 weeks with peering, Private = many weeks?
[08:32] Maya: That's a good summary. Hosted quickstart = minutes-hours (TTFT), Dedicated with VPC peering = ~1-2 weeks, Private/on-prem = multiple weeks and depends on infra approvals.
[08:45] Zoe: Any limits on model sizes for hosted?
[08:48] Carlos: We host many model sizes; very large models (100B+) are typically in Dedicated or Private due to GPU footprint, but we have optimized mid-size models in hosted.
[09:03] Priya: Can we do a short perf spike test using hosted to validate latency before committing to Dedicated?
[09:10] Maya: You can, but note hosted is multi-tenant so p95 might be less consistent. For a representative test we recommend a short Dedicated pilot, but we can do smoke tests on hosted to catch major blockers.
[09:25] Ben: For the quickstart, what's the expected token accounting? Any hidden charges?
[09:31] Maya: We'll provide a credits conversion sheet. No hidden charges beyond token/embedding usage in the plan; overages follow published rates unless under a reserved commit.
[09:44] Zoe: Another question: logging — do you provide request-level logs including prompts? Is that on by default?
[09:52] Carlos: By default we persist logs for a team-specific retention; you can opt out or redact. For security-sensitive teams, logs can be stored only in your VPC in Private deployments.
[10:06] Priya: Ok this is all helpful. Can you send an example curl to do streaming summarization?
[10:11] Carlos: Yes I'll include in the quickstart: a streaming endpoint example with chunked responses and reconnect handling.
[10:21] Maya: Recap on next steps — I'll send SOC2 + network diagram; Carlos will send quickstart repo and credits guide; Ben to send QPS/latency spreadsheet; Maya to coordinate perf demo scheduling.
[10:36] Ben: Sounds good. We might have some legal review on data residency later — expect a security call after we review docs.
[10:44] Priya: Timeline-wise we'll aim to redeem credits this week and have a dev test by early next week. If that works for Redwood we can try to hit the 3-week public beta.
[10:58] Maya: That aligns. We'll help prioritize the quickstart artifacts so you can get to first call fast.
[11:06] Zoe: One more thing — fallback policies: say the primary model is overloaded, will requests auto-failover to a smaller model?
[11:13] Carlos: Yes we can configure automatic fallback to a cheaper/compatible variant with slightly different prompts; useful for graceful degradation.
[11:23] Priya: Great. Anything else?
[11:26] Maya: No, thank you. We'll follow up with the docs and demo invite.
[11:31] Ben: Thanks all.

(End of meeting)
